instructions: Soak the glass noodles in a bowl of warm water for 5 minutes, then drain them and snip them into 3-inch pieces with scissors.
Soak the mushrooms in 1/2 cup hot water for 10 minutes, until soft. Lift them out, squeeze them and slice them thin. Keep the soaking water.
Meanwhile, slice the cabbage into thin strips and the green onions thin. Pound or mince the garlic into a paste with the coriander, white pepper and salt.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic paste and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the pork and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 4 minutes, until no pink is left. Add 2 tbsp of the fish sauce and the mushroom soaking water, leaving any grit in the bowl.
Pour in the broth and add the mushrooms and cabbage. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the noodles and simmer for 3 minutes, until they're clear and soft.
Stir in the soy sauce. Take the pot off the heat and stir in half the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Ladle into bowls and top with the rest of the green onions. Slice the chilies and juice the lime into a small dish with the remaining 2 tbsp fish sauce, and put it on the table for anyone who wants heat.
To store it, keep the soup in the fridge for up to 3 days or the freezer for up to 2 months. The noodles soften, so add a splash of broth when you reheat it.
method_notes: Import Food's bean vermicelli soup with pork leads (one review, no rating): garlic and pepper paste, pork cooked in it, dried shiitake and cabbage, then stock and noodles, with a fish sauce, lime and chili dip at the table. Cuisine Thailand's version has the same stock, fish sauce and soy base with the noodles added at the end. Broth is doubled to 6 cups to make a bigger pot, and the heat stays in the dip. Fallback.
